summary: This change adds published apps: an AppStore and AppService in the control plane, owner-side publication markers, idempotent installs on app VMs, an `apps` RPC namespace, and a `halo app` CLI. It is not ready. Binding integration actions rejects every real tool address, so two temp tests fail. Cancel cannot recover a publication whose app VM never answered. The coverage gate also fails: most new lines show as uncovered, likely because the failing control-plane temp run left no coverage for them.

findings.body: `validateActions` passes owner actions through `validateAppDefinition`. That function rejects any address whose first segment is in `reservedActionNamespaces`, and that set includes `tools`. Every real integration address starts with `tools.`, for example `tools.private-mcp.user.personal.echo_marker` in ControlPlane.test.ts:2990, and `connectPages` returns the same form. As a result, `apps.bindActions` and the `halo app bind-actions` command always fail with "actions must name connected integration operations". Both failing temp tests show this: publicationEdges.test.ts "owners bind fixed actions…" and cli.test.ts. The same check runs in `define()` (line ~359), so any package that declares `halo.app.actions` with a real tool is abandoned at publication. Fix the address check so it accepts the executor's real `tools.<integration>.<owner>.<connection>.<tool>` form and still rejects Halo's own namespaces (for example `tools.halo.*` and `tools.executor.*`). Rely on `integrations.describe` for the ownership check.

`cancel` handles a `frozen` app by calling `installedOnVm`. That function treats only a missing connection (`undefined`) as "not installed". `ExeWorkspaceProvider.getConnection` returns a connection as soon as the VM exists, whether or not its server listens. Take the case that cancel exists for: `waitForApp` timed out, or the app VM's server crashed. Then `client.extensions.list()` fails, `remoteFailure("probe")` returns an opaque `AppRemoteError`, and cancel always fails with an internal error. The owner's extension stays frozen. The only way out is a publish that also cannot succeed. Treat a failed probe as "not installed", or decide by whether the install-ID marker exists. In both cases, make sure the app VM cannot later receive the install. Also add a temp test for cancelling after the app VM is provisioned but unreachable, for example with `brokenOrigins`.

When `ensure()` has already provisioned an app VM but the install did not run (for example a timeout or a later failure), `cancel` → `abandon` deletes the app record. Nothing removes the provisioned VM, and `WorkspaceProviderApi` has no delete operation. The VM, named by the deleted `appId`, keeps running with no record that refers to it. Every publish-fail-cancel cycle leaks one VM, because the next attempt gets a new `appId`. Either deprovision the app VM on abandon (add a provider operation for it), or keep a tombstone so the orphaned VM can be found and removed.

testRequests.target: AppService.define with a package.json whose halo.app.actions names a real connected tool (tools.… address) publishes live and lists the action
testRequests.rationale: No passing test covers a declared action that validates successfully. The only declared-action test (publication.test.ts:89) checks rejection, and after the F1 fix it may pass for the wrong reason.

testRequests.target: AppService.cancel for a frozen app whose app VM exists but does not answer (getConnection returns an origin whose server is down)
testRequests.rationale: Covers the recovery path in F2. The current tests only cancel after `ensure` itself failed, when the VM has no connection.

testRequests.target: Coverage for packages/halo-cli/src/app.ts, AppService.ts, AppStore.ts, controlPlaneRpcRouter.ts apps handlers, creatorHost.ts, AppCredentials.ts, the Gcp and Exe provider changes, and appsRouter.ts forwarding
testRequests.rationale: These lines show as uncovered because the control-plane temp run failed. After F1 is fixed, rerun the run and confirm coverage. Add tests or accepted exemptions for any lines that are still uncovered, for example appsRouter.ts:26-29 (passing BAD_REQUEST through and rethrowing other errors).
